# Category tax verification (end to end, all categories)

**Status:** generated by `tools/taxonomy/verification_report.py` on 2026-11-10 from the matrix tests listed below. **Not tax or legal advice.** This proves the software does what the dataset says; it does not prove the dataset is right: that needs the Texas tax professional (see the last section). Do not edit this file by hand: re-run `make category-tax-verify`.

## Result

| | |
|---|---|
| Categories | **74 PASS, 0 FAIL** of 74 (73 from the dataset + the provisional Fabrics & textiles) |
| Decision rows (Appendix A scenarios) | 105, each run through resolve, the publish gate, a Texas quote and the order snapshot |
| Catalog publish gate runs | 109 (every row on the category's first product type, the first row on every other product type) |
| Texas checkout quotes | 191 (taxable lines in three ZIPs: 77002 8.25%, 78205 8.00%, 79401 6.25%; exempt and blocked lines in one) |
| Negative checks | 76 at catalog (each required fact removed, text in a number or a yes/no) and 85 at tax-returns |
| Individual assertion failures | 0 |
| Status gates | ACTIVE 57, BLOCKED_BUNDLE 1, CONFLICT_OPEN 2, NEEDS_APPROVAL 8, REFINE_CODE 6 |

## How it is verified

| Step | What | Where | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) build a valid minimal product through catalog's real validation | facts per variant, the seller's behaviour on the listing, required details, evidence uploaded where the rule needs proof | `CategoryTaxMatrixIT` (catalog) on the tree seeded by migration V20 in PostgreSQL | integration test (Testcontainers) |
| (b) publish gate | PENDING_REVIEW after submit (tax review required), READY once tax review approves, LIVE; gated categories refused or held; going live before approval refused | same | same |
| (c) resolve | outcome, internal code, Stripe code, status of every row | `CategoryTaxMatrixTest` (tax-returns), the real 73 profiles and the provider code map | unit test, real engine, in-memory ports |
| (d) checkout quote, Texas | EXEMPT 0; TAXABLE state 6.25% + local per the ZIP table (migration V4) on the discounted items and the delivery, rounded half up once per line; gated or missing: BLOCKED with the plain message and no rate | same | same |
| (e) order placement | the line snapshot (outcome, internal code, Stripe code, rule version, address precision, delivery share) and the order-placed line event; undecided lines stop the checkout with the plain message | `CategoryTaxMatrixTest` (orders) | unit test, the real checkout tax step, tax-returns' answer from the dataset |
| Implementations agree | the Python reference, tax-returns' evaluator and catalog's local resolver give the same decision on all 659 golden cases (105 scenarios, 440 fact combinations, 114 required facts removed) | `DecisionCasesTest`, `LocalDatasetTaxResolverGoldenTest`, `tools/taxonomy/decision_cases.py --check` | unit tests |

The quote and the order steps use fakes at the HTTP edges (tax-returns is not called over HTTP from orders here): the shapes of those calls are held by `PublicVariantContractTest` / `HttpProductFactsContractTest` / `HttpProductFactsClientTest` (catalog's public variant, which tax-returns and orders read) and by the conformance tests of each contract. Nothing here drives a browser.

## Commands to re-run

```bash
make category-tax-verify                      # everything below, then rewrites this file (catalog's IT needs Docker)
make category-tax-verify CATALOG_IT=0         # skip the catalog IT (no Docker); the report then needs its JSON from an earlier run

make taxonomy-check                           # dataset, decision cases, reference evaluator
cd java && ./mvnw -pl services/tax-returns test -Dtest='DecisionCasesTest,CategoryTaxMatrixTest'
cd java && ./mvnw -pl services/orders test -Dtest=CategoryTaxMatrixTest
cd java && ./mvnw -pl services/catalog test -Dtest=LocalDatasetTaxResolverGoldenTest
cd java && ./mvnw -pl services/catalog verify -Dit.test=CategoryTaxMatrixIT -Dtest=NoUnitTests -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false   # Docker
python3 tools/taxonomy/verification_report.py
```

## Per category

Form fields: tax questions, proof (evidence file) questions and detail questions of the category's first product type. Negative checks: required facts removed and wrong-type answers tried (catalog plus tax-returns). Outcomes verified are the dataset's: EXEMPT and TAXABLE rows were quoted and snapshotted, the others were verified to block.

## Real defects the matrix found, and their fixes

Found while wiring the four independently tested parts together (all fixed in this change; each has a test that fails without the fix):

1. **Catalog could not start.** The tree seed was a Java Flyway migration that extended `BaseJavaMigration`, which refuses class names that do not start with V or R; the service failed at start-up. The tree is now plain generated SQL in the catalog baseline (`V1_1__initial_data.sql`, `tools/taxonomy/gen_catalog_baseline.py`), so no Java migration remains.
2. **No product could ever pass the tax gate.** Products sit on a product-type node, but the tax profile and status live on the category above it; the gate read the product type's (empty) profile and answered NEEDS_APPROVAL for everything, and no tax event was published. Unit tests had faked a profile on the leaf. Product types now read their category's profile and status (`JdbcCategoryRepository.findById`), and a status change reaches their products (`findByTaxProfile`). Caught by `CategoryTaxMatrixIT` on the real tree.
3. **tax-returns read the wrong part of catalog's answer.** Its on-the-fly lookup read `taxFacts` and the category from the root of `GET /v1/public/variants/{atin}`, but they sit under `variant` and `product`; and catalog returned no category code or listing behaviour at all. Catalog now returns `product.categoryCode` and `product.listing.sellerBehaviour`; tax-returns reads `variant.taxFacts`, `product.categoryCode`, `product.listing.sellerBehaviour` and `product.sellerOrgId` (the behaviour stays with the owner's listing). Held by one fixture, `contracts/examples/catalog-public-variant.json`, read by catalog's, tax-returns' and orders' tests.
4. **Checkout never told tax-returns the seller's behaviour or the order.** Orders now sends `orderId` and each line's `sellerBehaviour` (from the owner's catalog listing, never another seller's); a category that needs it and does not get it blocks the line (MISSING_FACTS). The order-placed line event now carries `taxAddressPrecision`, which the tax ledger reads.
5. **Stored product types failed to load.** The starter `custom` and `electronics` types lack the `taxFact` and `evidence` flags and failed to read; absent now reads as false.
6. **Deployed services could not reach each other for tax.** Orders had no tax-returns address outside local (`localhost`), catalog had none for its resolver and did not request the `tax:classify` scope: every checkout and every publish would have failed in dev, uat and prod. Fixed, and `tools/ci/check_env_config.py` now checks it. Orders' perishable product types and commission categories still named the retired tree (`perishable`, `grocery`); they now name the new product types.
7. **Kafka ACL:** catalog consumes `at.taxreturns.events` but was not listed as a consumer.

## Known limits, by design (not failures)

- **Tax holiday calendar not built (TX-08).** Rows that need an active exemption window (car seats, scenario 73) resolve as the dataset says, but a quote prices the ordinary sale of the category: always the taxable direction.
- **ZIP rates, not exact addresses (TX-03).** Every quote line records `addressPrecision = ZIP`. A ZIP can span several local jurisdictions; this is the documented launch limitation.
- **Delivery attribution for mixed baskets (TX-07)** is the proportional allocation, an owner decision still open; **bundles (TX-09)** and **platform fee classification (TX-12)** are not built.
- **Seller is a bakery** is asked of the seller as part of "Your listing"; the seller profile flag (planned migration V89) does not exist yet.
- **Not run here:** the browser forms, Stripe or Avalara calls, the real Kafka path between catalog, tax-returns and orders, the HTTP calls between services (held by contract tests instead), mobile checkout.

## What still needs a human

1. **Browser pass of every category form** in Seller Center (Add product), with the product form's "Price & stock" and "Your listing" wording. The 13 department forms to walk through: Baby & Kids; Beauty & Personal Care; Beverages; Books & Media; Digital Products; Electronics; Fashion & Accessories; Groceries & Food; Health & Wellness; Home & Household; Other & Specialty; Pets; Services. Plus the special groups that need their own pass:
   - heated food and utensils (`sold_heated`, `heated_by_seller`, `utensils_provided`, `seller_is_bakery`): prepared meals, bakery products, ready-to-drink coffee and tea;
   - label type (Nutrition Facts or Supplement Facts) for beverages, supplements and packaged food;
   - live versus recorded (event tickets, fitness classes, tutoring, online courses), and printed versus digital books and media;
   - bundles and gift baskets (blocked) and gift cards (held);
   - evidence upload: label photo, Drug Facts, Supplement Facts (PDF, JPEG or PNG up to 10 MB), the readiness block and its plain messages, and the staff tax review screens (Sales tax in the sidebar).
